title: Intrinsic orientation and regularity entering the characteristic set
source_hypothesis: Scalar proper classical P of real order m satisfying (P), regular characteristic curves. Entering: a regular real semibicharacteristic has initially negative Im(qp), q nonzero, and Pu microlocally Hs on its compact interval. Starting-point: a compact characteristic interval in N11 has Pu Hs throughout and u H(s+m-1) at its intrinsic starting point. Propagated order s+m-1; elliptic points retain order s+m.
reviewed_arguments: A compact rank-one characteristic interval in N11 is carried to an accessible endpoint within the regular domain. Exact flow uniqueness, no-return and radial arguments justify a common embedded cosphere interval; endpoints where dp vanishes are not included.

The current complete complex normal-form and condition-(P) geometry proofs give one common homogeneous tube, a tau-independent imaginary part of fixed sign and strict central values approaching the accessible endpoint. The singleton zero component uses the exact point construction.

For every smooth nonzero multiplier ratio A+iB, including tau-dependent ones, its real zero surface is an implicit graph and its imaginary part there is exactly (A squared+B squared)f/A. The real Hamilton direction is A times the marked time direction. Strict endpoint values exclude the opposite orientation.

The definition uses an endpoint-maximal interval and restricts to shorter intervals. A common normal form and condition (P) prove agreement for different accessible extensions; a locally real interior piece alone does not choose an orientation.

The full operator reduction uses an elliptic left factor of order 1-m and proper order-zero graph quantizations with both inverse errors. Ordered Egorov retains all lower terms. Finite overlapping graph patches avoid presuming a global Maslov frame.

The microlocal distribution identities retain larger cutoffs, proper action and graph wavefront localization. The transformed forcing has order s+m-1, and both graph factors preserve every real Sobolev order.

For entering propagation, connected characteristic-time components may be singletons or occur infinitely often. The initially negative value and condition (P) supply negative noncharacteristic points approaching the left endpoint.

The original real orbit need not equal the new normal-form central line outside the characteristic component. The exact zero-surface formula transfers its sign; flow uniqueness separately supplies a negative central elliptic point within the actual forcing neighborhood.

Ellipticity at that nearby point gives the stronger order s+m. Ordinary propagation then gives s+m-1 through the component. Openness and a finite subcover complete the whole compact orbit without assuming finitely many zero components.

The starting-point theorem uses a farther accessible endpoint only for geometry. All analytic propagation takes place in the forcing neighborhood of the stated compact interval, so no unassumed far-endpoint regularity is imposed.

Fixed-cone smooth propagation is transferred with the exact ordinary fixed-cone theorem and graph wavefront relations; separate neighborhoods for each Sobolev order are not mistaken for smooth regularity.

Three complete solutions check a rotating multiplier, arbitrary operator order and opposite entering/exiting flat geometries. Both symbol and conjugate tests establish condition (P) in the model. Twenty exact symbolic identities passed.

The ordinary sign estimate is the operator input for the invariant results here. The complex-cutoff theorem treats shrinking measurements, and positive Fourier packets realize prescribed concave indices with their exact wavefront ray.
